content.title: About
content.content: Cheese roll is a small round snack made from soft dough filled with processed cheese. It is popular as a quick bite and is often served in cafés, cafeterias, and retail stores. The dough is usually tender with a slight crisp, while the filling is smooth and aromatic.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cheese rolls originated in Japan as a variant of "cheese dumplings" and quickly spread worldwide.
They are commonly made with wheat flour, but whole‑grain and gluten‑free versions also exist.
In some countries they are served with soy‑based or sweet chili dipping sauces.
Cheese rolls are conveniently packaged in single‑serve packs, making them popular for office snacks.
Variants with herbs, spices or smoked cheese add extra flavor diversity.

items.title: Source of protein
items.content: Cheese provides high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Calcium
items.content: Cheese roll supplies calcium, important for bone and tooth health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Cheese is rich in B2 and B12 vitamins, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Dietary fiber (in the dough)
items.content: When made with whole‑grain flour, the roll adds dietary fiber that aids digestion.

items.title: Energy boost
items.content: The combination of carbohydrates from the dough and fats from the cheese provides a quick source of energy.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Cheese roll contains lactose, so people with intolerance should choose lactose‑free versions.

items.title: High salt content
items.content: Cheese is often salty; excessive intake may raise blood pressure.

items.title: Milk‑protein allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to casein.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: The mix of dough and cheese makes the roll calorie‑dense, so portion control is advised.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Ready‑made rolls may contain additives; opt for products without artificial preservatives when possible.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cheese rolls can be eaten cold as a snack, warmed in a microwave or oven until golden, and pair well with sauces such as tomato, mustard, creamy, or soy. For a lighter bite, they are often served alongside vegetable sticks.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store rolls in an airtight container in the refrigerator at 2‑4 °C for up to 5 days. For longer storage, freeze them in a freezer‑safe bag for up to 2 months. Before eating, reheat at 180 °C in the oven for 5‑7 minutes.
